newsitem.title: UK: UK grains market stays firm despite stg strength.
newsitem.headline: UK grains market stays firm despite stg strength.

text.p: Despite a soaring pound, the UK's grains market remains firm with a widespread perception that it is not as well, or over, supplied as once thought.
"The way things are going in the UK, we can use most of the wheat we've got, if not all," one trader said.
Positive sentiment has helped LIFFE futures fight back against the strong pound, with the May wheat contract coming back from a low of 93.00 stg on Feb 12 to a day's high of 100.00 stg Wednesday.
The view that farmers are not selling as much as all the other market players would like is universal.
But there is less agreement about the other side of the equation.
"We feel at the moment the market is shipper led," one of the UK's biggest grain consumers said.
"It's domestic," a leading shipper said. "Consumers want to take a bit of cover, particularly on April/May/June."

Demand from shippers is all for business already booked, he said. "OK, the French market has gone firm in the last few days. It means the UK could do a bit of extra business, but nothing untoward," he said.
"The basis of this market is merchant buying," he said.
Farmers have been selling a bit, at their usual level of around 95 stg ex-farm," he said.
A feed compounder buyer disagreed. "People (consumers) are fairly well covered on the nearbys; April, May, June and in some cases July," he said.
"In the short term positions most people are fairly well bought up," he said. "By going forward they're protecting their feed costs at the end of the year."
He reckoned farmer selling was still limited. The response of many traditional minded farmers in current circumstances was to "shut the barn door on a rising market," he said.

According to the Home Grown Cereals Authority, UK traders expected wheat exports to reach between 3.3 and 3.5 million tonnes by the end of March, compared to just under 2.6 million by the same stage last year.
